reply_cache.role: NOT read by the replay. Used once, for provenance: its primary key is sha256(model \0 max_tokens \0 system \0 user \0), so the prompt text of the run that produced the results file is recoverable by reconstruction. See `provenance` below.

provenance.confidence: cryptographic -- not inferred from filenames, mtimes or README prose
provenance.method: go_council.py:212 CallCache.key() hashes (model, str(max_tokens), system, user), each NUL-terminated, with SHA-256, and go_council.py:272 stores every reply under that key in the .cache.sqlite sidecar. The prompts of the ACTUAL run are therefore recoverable: reconstruct each call's (model, system, user) from a candidate generator's prompt constants plus the recorded input, hash it, and test membership in the sidecar's key set. A generator whose prompts differ by one byte produces a different key and matches nothing.

evidence.v3_kit_total: 433 of 434 reconstructed keys present -- i.e. EVERY one of the 433 cache rows is accounted for
evidence.the_single_miss: input_id 5540, seat gemini35flash, role proposer. That call raised (ValueError: no JSON object in: ...) and go_council.py:291-292 only writes the cache AFTER a successful parse, so it was never cached. The miss is explained by the record itself, not by a prompt difference.
evidence.pilot_cross_check: 0 of 300 -- the 09-18 LIVE pilot /scratch/jplfaria/CONCORDIA-live/scripts/go_council_pilot.py (PROPOSER_SYSTEM carrying the extra candidate-provenance rules) matches NOTHING in this cache.
evidence.corroborating: The results rows carry exactly the 12 keys go_council.py:482-491 `run_one` returns, and the cache's per-(model, phase) row counts -- gpt54/gpt55 proposer 100 each, gemini35flash proposer 99, claudesonnet5 critic 100, claudeopus45 meta 34 -- match the roster at go_council.py:46-48 and the 34 meta-run rows in the results file.

provenance.consequence: results_strat100_jose_v3.jsonl was produced by the V3 KIT, which is the same file go_mf@1 ports. The oracle and the implementation under test share a prompt lineage, so this replay is a genuine parity check rather than a comparison across two different queries. No change to go_mf@1 is warranted.

expected_differences.note: The ONLY permitted expected-difference predicates, each evaluated mechanically over all 100 recorded rows by scripts/council/replay_go_v3.py. A row not listed here is held to exact semantic parity.

b_proposer_error_then_critic_or_meta.predicate: any('error' in reply for reply in row['proposers'].values()) and (row['critic'] or row['meta'])
b_proposer_error_then_critic_or_meta.note: Not a second row: the only recorded proposer error is the one in the only recorded error row. V3 continued to critic and meta after gemini35flash failed; the council stops at the failed proposer by design (engine/decide.py step 3).

c_off_menu_or_duplicate_pick.predicate: for each non-errored proposer reply, any picked go_id absent from that row's candidate menu, or any go_id appearing twice in one reply
c_off_menu_or_duplicate_pick.note: EMPTY, and structurally so for the off-menu half: go_council.py:314-318 already filters each proposer's picks to the offered set before recording, so an off-menu id cannot survive into the record. The duplicate half is not filtered by the kit (go_council.py:337 increments once per pick, so a repeat would count twice where the council counts once) -- it simply did not occur in these 100 rows.

normalisation.why: Eight recorded replies do not satisfy go_mf@1's answer schema, which Jose's V3 runner did not enforce. engine/normalise.py repairs exactly those two defects before the gate and records every repair on calls.normalised and on the verdict (normalised + per-seat repairs). The raw reply text is unchanged and every other schema failure is still invalid_output.

derived_content_flag.rule: a meta reply missing no_functional_content gets it: False when its final ids list is non-empty, else the value decide()'s skip-path content rule gives (proposer majority 2t>n -> True, 2t<n -> False, tie -> the critic's contentless_input)
derived_content_flag.note: All seven name a non-empty final_go_ids, so all seven take the first branch; the skip-path branch is not reached by this transcript and is covered by tests/domains/ai/council/test_normalise.py instead.

null_string.rule: a property the role's answer schema types as string whose value is None becomes "" (including inside picked[])

normalisation.rule_only_control: The decision rule alone agreed on all 8 of these rows BEFORE normalisation existed, and still does (the report keeps the rule-only column). A repair that changed a decision rather than merely admitting one would show as the rule-only and end-to-end columns disagreeing.

comparison.rationale: Prompt text, reply wording, token usage and id ORDER are not compared. Order differs by design and not by disagreement: the V3 runner reports the skip path's ids in first-vote order (go_council.py:383) and the meta path's in the order meta named them (go_council.py:449-451), while engine/decide.py reports both in MENU order.
